title: Building your syllabus
blurb: Sign in, open the editor, turn a Word document into a syllabus, and publish it.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Go to Teacher sign-in and enter your school email and password. If your school is using the shared admin password instead of individual accounts, leave the email blank.

steps.title: Find your class on the Classes page
steps.body: Every class you teach is a row here, with how many students are active, dropped, registered, and holding an access code. Syllabus opens the editor below; Who has signed and Access codes are covered in the rest of this guide.

steps.title: Open the syllabus editor
steps.body: A brand new class opens straight to "Start from a document," because there is nothing in the draft yet to show instead. The editor works one page at a time — the same page a parent turns to — with Fix headings, Suggest initials, Save draft, and Publish along the top. Nothing here is visible to parents until you publish it.

steps.title: Start from a document
steps.body: Drop a .docx here, or paste text straight from Word or Google Docs — the box grows to fit whatever you paste. Pasted text is split into blocks automatically: a short line with no punctuation becomes a heading, everything else becomes a paragraph or a list.

steps.title: Choose the AI model in Settings
steps.body: The gear icon next to Sign out holds one setting: which AI model answers Fix headings and Suggest initials. Your choice is remembered on this computer.

steps.title: Fix headings straightens out the structure
steps.body: A pasted document often has real headings that do not look like headings to a simple rule — a title that ends with a period, or a line that got bolded instead of styled. Fix headings asks an AI model to tell headings from body text and retags them. It never rewrites a word; only the tag around a line ever changes.

steps.title: Suggest initials flags sections worth a signature
steps.body: This asks the same model which sections a parent should have to initial individually — grading and late work, attendance, safety, academic honesty, anything that costs money. Suggestions show up as a note in the margin; nothing is required until you click Require initials on a page yourself.

steps.title: Edit text and add a block
steps.body: Double-click any line to place a cursor and type. Below the page, "Add to this page" adds a paragraph, a list, a subheading, or an initials box wherever you are reading.

steps.title: Reorder or delete a block
steps.body: Click a block once to pick it up, then drag it — or use the ↑ / ↓ arrows to nudge it a line at a time. The ✕ on the right deletes it. A heading carries its whole page with it when you drag it; a loose line moves on its own.

steps.title: Save draft keeps it private
steps.body: Save draft writes your changes to the server, but nothing changes for parents — they still see whatever was last published. Save often; there is no autosave, and the page warns you before you navigate away with unsaved changes.

steps.title: Review what changed before publishing
steps.body: This class already has a published syllabus and an open draft with real edits: a softened late-work policy, and a new Tutoring and Extra Help page. Read through a draft before publishing it — Publish shows you a count of what changed, but not the actual wording.

steps.title: Publish when it is ready
steps.body: Publishing asks you to confirm how many sections are new or changed, how many are unchanged, and how many changed sections require initials — then makes the new version live immediately. Anyone who already initialed a section that changed now shows as having signed an older version and has to initial it again, even if the change was small.
